claims.text: Increasing compositional complexity to five or more principal elements increases configurational entropy relative to a binary or ternary composition.
High configurational entropy produces significant local fluctuations in surface bond energies in HEA nanoparticles.
Surface-bond-energy fluctuations cause premelting to begin earlier in HEA nanoparticles.
Surface-bond-energy fluctuations cause premelting to proceed more gradually in HEA nanoparticles.
The appropriate baseline is a binary or ternary nanoparticle alloy with average bonding energy matched to that of the HEA.
The HEA and baseline nanoparticles can be prepared as comparable-size, single-phase disordered solid solutions.
The HEA nanoparticles possess greater atomic-scale heterogeneity than the binary or ternary baseline nanoparticles.
Random occupation by multiple element types creates a distribution of local bonding strengths and surface binding energies.
Surface regions with lower local binding energy disorder at lower temperatures than more strongly bound regions.
The progressive disordering of differently bound surface regions generates graded premelting.
Reduced-complexity baseline alloys have comparatively uniform bonding.
Reduced-complexity baseline nanoparticles undergo a sharper transition at a higher temperature than HEA nanoparticles.
HEA nanoparticles will have a statistically lower onset temperature for surface disorder than the matched baseline.
HEA nanoparticles will exhibit a broader or more gradual premelting interval in TEM and DSC than the matched baseline.
In situ high-resolution TEM and DSC can capture the proposed premelting and complete-melting transitions.
Size-dependent surface effects are prominent for the proposed nanoparticles below 50 nm.
The proposed behavior should hold under rapid thermal ramps in inert atmospheres.
The behavior may deviate for larger particles or under different environmental or heating conditions.
Synthesis variability and particle-size heterogeneity may alter the onset temperature and apparent gradation of premelting.
